description: We want to be trail blazers in interplanetary travel
summary:
The Permanent Moon Base & Mars Analog Finder, developed by Team Via Nebula for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, is an intelligent GIS platform designed to support sustainable long-term space colonization.

Space agencies currently lack integrated terrestrial test environments that accurately replicate harsh lunar polar shadows and Martian terrain. To solve this, the platform combines machine learning algorithms with NASA open datasets—specifically Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO/LOLA) altimetry and Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO) data—to analyze thermal profiles, topography, and solar illumination.

Built using Python, Pandas, and Leaflet.js, the current interactive web prototype allows space agencies, researchers, and habitat planners to select Earth locations and compare extraterrestrial match metrics in milliseconds. Future development plans include integrating 3D virtual reality simulations to enable realistic testing of surface exploration rovers within these identified terrestrial analogs.
details:
The Permanent Moon Base & Mars Analog Finder, created by Team Via Nebula for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge in Tabuk, is an intelligent GIS platform designed to identify terrestrial locations that mirror extraterrestrial environments.

How It Works

The platform bridges the gap between Earth geology and space exploration through a four-step pipeline:

  1. Data Ingestion: It imports orbital models from NASA Earthdata and the Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter (LOLA).
  2. Data Filtering: It processes and filters terrain geometry alongside solar illumination angles.
  3. Site Classification: Machine learning algorithms match Earth terrain against extraterrestrial data to build an accurate site-matching model.
  4. Interactive Output: The system generates an interactive analog map where users can select locations on Earth and compare space match metrics in milliseconds.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Solves the Testing Gap: Space agencies currently lack fully integrated, reliable ground test environments that accurately replicate harsh lunar polar shadows and Martian terrain to evaluate habitat sustainability.
  • Target Beneficiaries: The tool directly supports space agencies, geological researchers, and planetary habitat planners.
  • Long-Term Vision: By pairing Earth geological analogs with NASA orbital data, the project supports sustainable, long-term space colonization on the Moon and Mars. Future iterations will incorporate 3D virtual reality simulations to test surface exploration rovers within these analogous environments.

Tools, Languages & Datasets

  • Coding & Libraries: Python and Pandas for data processing and machine learning modeling.
    • NASA LRO & LOLA Altimetry: Used for Lunar South Pole topography and permanently shadowed region (PSR) mapping.
    • Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO): Used for high-resolution surface morphology and mineralogical analog data.

Creativity & Factors Considered

  • Novel Approach: Rather than relying solely on manual geological surveys, the project integrates machine learning algorithms directly with NASA open datasets for precise, rapid site classification.
  • Core Environmental Factors: To ensure accurate matches for Moon and Mars habitats, the team specifically analyzed thermal profiles, surface topography, mineralogical morphology, and solar illumination angles.
